name: endpoints-create-hijack-procA
why: Procedure A: a non-controller (kubernetes-admin) create of a selectorless Service's core Endpoints (objectRef.resource=endpoints, core group so no objectRef.apiGroup, verb=create) -- the actor-class chokepoint. On a Metadata record the hijack and a benign manual write look the same (the attacker-chosen address is in the body, which Metadata does not carry; K69).
source: real: local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab, atomics/T1557/src/emulate.sh, audit policy audit-policy-apiserver.yaml (endpoints/endpointslices writes fall to the Metadata catch-all) a

name: endpointslice-create-hijack-procB
why: Procedure B: a non-controller create of a discovery.k8s.io EndpointSlice (objectRef.resource=endpointslices, objectRef.apiGroup=discovery.k8s.io, verb=create) -- the discovery branch of the chokepoint.
source: real: local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab, atomics/T1557/src/emulate.sh, audit policy audit-policy-apiserver.yaml (endpoints/endpointslices writes fall to the Metadata catch-all) b

name: endpoints-update-hijack
why: a non-controller update (PUT) of an existing manual Endpoints repointing its addresses -- covers the update verb branch.
source: real: local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab, atomics/T1557/src/emulate.sh, audit policy audit-policy-apiserver.yaml (endpoints/endpointslices writes fall to the Metadata catch-all) a (repoint)

name: endpointslice-patch-hijack
why: a non-controller patch of a discovery.k8s.io EndpointSlice -- covers the patch verb on the discovery branch.
source: real: local kube-apiserver v1.36.4 lab, atomics/T1557/src/emulate.sh, audit policy audit-policy-apiserver.yaml (endpoints/endpointslices writes fall to the Metadata catch-all) b (repoint)

name: endpoints-create-failed-authentication
why: an endpoints create whose request failed authentication (401): the record has no user.username (apiserver v1.36.4 WithFailedAuthenticationAudit), so each identity filter's operand is NULL; sel_no_username guards the negations so the record still fires (null safety). A pure-surface chokepoint with no response-code gate fires on the attempt.
source: synthetic (the 401 shape apiserver writes for a failed-authentication create: no user, code 401)

name: endpoint-controller-endpoints-update
why: the endpoint controller updates a selector Service's core Endpoints from its Ready pods (kubernetes v1.36.4 pkg/controller/endpoint); its service account is filtered. Every selection holds (endpoints, no apiGroup, update), so only user.username suppresses it; changing the username alone fires the rule. This same suppression is the K69 stolen-token evasion.
source: synthetic (a controller Endpoints update as kubeadm's per-SA controller manager sends it)

name: endpointslice-controller-endpointslices-update
why: the endpointslice controller updates a selector Service's EndpointSlices (kubernetes v1.36.4 pkg/controller/endpointslice); its service account is filtered. Every selection holds (endpointslices, discovery.k8s.io, update), so only user.username suppresses it.
source: synthetic (a controller EndpointSlice update, kubeadm per-SA controller manager)

name: endpointslicemirroring-controller-endpointslices-create
why: the endpointslicemirroring controller mirrors a hand-written Endpoints into an EndpointSlice (kubernetes v1.36.4 pkg/controller/endpointslicemirroring); its service account is filtered. Every selection holds (endpointslices, discovery.k8s.io, create), so only user.username suppresses it. This is the controller that reacts to Procedure A's manual Endpoints, so its own mirror write must stay quiet.
source: synthetic (a mirroring-controller EndpointSlice create for a selectorless Service)

name: kube-controller-manager-endpoints-update
why: with --use-service-account-credentials=false every controller acts as the controller manager's own identity, so its Endpoints writes carry user.username system:kube-controller-manager; that identity is filtered. Every selection holds (endpoints, no apiGroup, update), so only user.username suppresses it.
source: synthetic (an Endpoints update by a controller manager run without per-SA credentials)

name: endpoints-deletecollection-namespace-teardown
why: a namespace teardown deletecollections a namespace's endpoints (the namespace controller when a namespace is deleted), which the rule deliberately does not match: a deletecollection removes addresses rather than repointing them, and it is routine (the benign corpus carries it). Changing verb to create/update/patch alone fires the rule (the namespace controller is not an endpoint-controller filter), so the write-verb set is load-bearing.
source: synthetic (a namespace-controller endpoints deletecollection, as in detections/benign/slices/kubernetes/k8s-audit-gitops-ci.json)

name: custom-endpoints-crd-other-apigroup
why: a create of a custom resource whose plural is 'endpoints' in a non-core API group (objectRef.apiGroup=example.com): it shares the resource surface but is not the core Endpoints object, so objectRef.apiGroup is present and sel_core_endpoints (which requires the apiGroup absent) does not hold. Proves the core/CRD apiGroup discriminator: a look-alike CRD does not fire.
source: synthetic (a CRD named endpoints in group example.com, logged at the Metadata catch-all)

name: endpoint-controller-token-stolen-known-miss
why: KNOWN MISS (RULE_DEFECTS.md K69): an Endpoints update sent with a STOLEN endpoint-controller service-account token is filtered by identity, so the rule does not fire -- a credential-theft evasion, the class of K37/K50/K51. The filter is kept because the controller rewrites these objects on every pod-readiness change; without it every real hit would be buried. It shares the rule's surface (an endpoints update that every selection matches) and is suppressed only by the username filter.
source: synthetic (a hijack sent as the endpoint controller's identity, the filtered evasion)

name: apiserver-reconciler-default-kubernetes-endpoints-update
why: the API server's own endpoint reconciler (the lease/EndpointReconciler) updates the selectorless default/kubernetes Service's core Endpoints under the loopback identity system:apiserver -- the one selectorless Service no endpoint/endpointslice/mirroring controller manages, so it is reconciled by the apiserver itself, not a controller. Every selection holds (endpoints, no apiGroup, update), so only user.username suppresses it; changing the username alone fires the rule. Without this filter every apiserver restart, HA lease change or apiserver IP change that rewrites default/kubernetes would fire -- the K69 token-trust class (an attacker holding the apiserver loopback credential has already won).
source: synthetic (the kube-apiserver endpoint reconciler's default/kubernetes Endpoints update under its loopback identity system:apiserver)
